# Valkarn Tasks

> Zero-allocation, struct-based async/await framework for Unity.
> Faster than UniTask. Source-generated lifecycle cancellation. Burst & ECS ready.

Valkarn Tasks is a Unity package providing a high-performance async/await implementation
that avoids heap allocations on the happy path, auto-cancels tasks when MonoBehaviours
are destroyed (via source generator), integrates with Unity Burst and ECS, and ships
17 Roslyn analyzer rules that catch async bugs at compile time.

License: Free for individuals and studios under $1M/year revenue.
Commercial license: https://tasks.valkarn.com/licensing

## Getting Started

- [Migration from UniTask](https://tasks.valkarn.com/docs/migration-from-unitask): Valkarn Tasks is API-compatible with UniTask in most common cases. This guide covers the differences.

- [Unity PlayerLoop Integration](https://tasks.valkarn.com/docs/concepts/player-loop): ValkarnTasks does not use threads or background schedulers to resume your async methods. Everything runs on Unity's main thread, driven by Unity's own PlayerLoop system. Understand
- [Auto-Cancel Lifecycle Binding](https://tasks.valkarn.com/docs/concepts/auto-cancel): One of the most common bugs in Unity async code is launching a task from a MonoBehaviour and then forgetting to cancel it when the object is destroyed. The task continues running, 
## API Reference

- [ValkarnTask](https://tasks.valkarn.com/docs/api/vlk-task): ValkarnTask is the core awaitable type. It is a readonly struct — no heap allocation on the happy path (when the task completes synchronously or via pool).
- [ValkarnTask<T>](https://tasks.valkarn.com/docs/api/vlk-task-t): ValkarnTask<T> is the value-returning async task type in Valkarn Tasks. It is a readonly struct, carrying either an inline result (when synchronously completed) or a reference to a poo
- [Completion Sources](https://tasks.valkarn.com/docs/api/completion-source): ValkarnTaskCompletionSource<T> and the non-generic ValkarnTaskCompletionSource give you manual control over a ValkarnTask. They are the async equivalent of writing the result yourself — you ho
- [Channels](https://tasks.valkarn.com/docs/api/channels): Channels provide a thread-safe, async-capable pipeline for passing data between producers and consumers. They are particularly suited to game systems where work is generated on one
- [PlayerLoopTiming](https://tasks.valkarn.com/docs/api/player-loop-timing): public enum PlayerLoopTiming : byte
- [Settings & Result](https://tasks.valkarn.com/docs/api/settings): ValkarnTaskSettings is a Unity ScriptableObject that controls the runtime behavior of Valkarn Tasks — primarily the object pool that recycles async state machines and promise objects t

- [Analyzer Rules](https://tasks.valkarn.com/docs/advanced/analyzers): Valkarn Tasks ships two Roslyn analyzer packages that activate automatically when the package is imported:
- [IL2CPP Compatibility](https://tasks.valkarn.com/docs/advanced/il2cpp): Valkarn Tasks is designed to work correctly under IL2CPP from the ground up. This page describes every measure taken and what you need to do — or not do — to ship safely on IL2CPP 
- [Testing](https://tasks.valkarn.com/docs/advanced/testing): Valkarn Tasks ships a dedicated testing infrastructure that lets you write fast, deterministic unit tests for async code — no real timers, no frame waits, no Unity Editor required
